subject: Funny histogram of body temperatures coming out of ecto

messages.author: 33b794434900b72b
messages.subject: Funny histogram of body temperatures coming out of ecto
parts:
Dear Michael,

When running micro and ecto for different locations at North America, I keep getting a histogram of body temperatures(tc) from ecto$environ that seem a bit unexpected to me:

values over CTmax are more frequent than values right over VTmax. I wonder how could this happen even for the case when I allow the lizard to find a reasonably deep burrow under the shade.  My first thought was that I was leaving any parameter in an unreasonable level, but after tweaking around, I could not find which it could be. Maybe the animal is bouncing back to the surface and frying there, when it reaches its VTMAx in the burrow, but how reasonable that can be for so deep burrows (2m deep)? Also, for such a hot place, the most frequent body temperatures go pretty under the preferred ones, might these be body temperatures during the night?

Here is my code and and the resultant histogram of body temperatures. Thank you very much for your time and for this splendid tool!
lon= -109.3458
lat= 28.4375
        micro=  micro_global(loc = c(lon,lat),
                    timeinterval=timeinterval,
                    nyears=nyears,
                    Usrhyt=0.004 ,
                    soiltype=2,
                    REFL= 0.1,                  
                    slope= 0,
                    aspect= 30,
                    DEP=c(0,2,5,10,15,30,60,90,100,120),
                    minshade= 10,
                    maxshade= 100,
                    RUF = 0.004,
                    PCTWET = 100,
                    CMH2O = 1,
                    runmoist=1
)

  ectotherm(
  Ww_g= 3 #
  ,shape= 3#
  ,T_F_max =42#
  ,T_pref= 35#
  ,T_B_min=20
  ,T_RB_min=20
  ,CT_max=45#
  ,CT_min=0
  ,climb=1
  ,shade_seek=1
  ,burrow  = 1
  ,shdburrow = 1
  ,mindepth    = 1 #
  ,maxdepth    = 7 #
  ,M_1    = 2.454#
  ,M_2    = 0.800#
  ,M_3    = 0.038#
  ,CT_kill = 0
  )

t=as.data.frame(ecto$environ[,c(1:5)])
hist(t$TC)

messages.author: e46cb5dd353b7dfb
messages.subject: Re: Funny histogram of body temperatures coming out of ecto
parts:
Dear Agus,

Glad you're enjoying playing with the models!

I can see where the problem is - you have a value of 2.454 for the parameter M_1, which is one of the three coefficients for the response of metabolic rate to temperature and body mass. This results in a metabolic rate almost 200 times what it would be for a lizard :). That's why they are getting so hot, especially as body temperature rises. Note also that you should not have a value for the Usrhyt parameter (local height you're simulating with the microclimate model) that is lower than the roughness height parameter RUF, because otherwise the microclimate model won't run. The parameter settings you have posted above for the microclimate model returns an error.

In general, when you see something odd happening, it can help to systematically delete your parameter specifications (and thereby let them be the default value), to help figure out what is causing the issue.

All the best,
Mike
